headlines.article_text: DoorDash's deal to buy Instacart coming as early as Thursday morning, sources tell CNBC Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points DoorDash's bid to buy Instacart could be announced as early as Thursday morning, CNBC has learned. In this article DASH Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 1:02 01:02 DoorDash deal to buy Instacart to be announced as early as Thursday morning Closing Bell: Overtime DoorDash 's bid to buy Instacart could be announced as soon as Thursday morning, sources familiar with the matter told CNBC. Speculation of a deal has swirled since last week, when The Information reported Instacart was exploring a sale and had held talks with companies including Uber and DoorDash. On Monday, several outlets reported DoorDash was in advanced discussions to acquire Instacart and that the deal could value Instacart at about $17 billion. Instacart's stock popped about 4% in extended trading on Wednesday, while DoorDash shares fell less than 1%. Instacart declined to comment. Representatives from DoorDash didn't immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment. Acquiring Instacart would give DoorDash a bigger presence in online grocery delivery. DoorDash got its start in food delivery, and since then it has added more retailers to its marketplace, such as Sephora, Macy's , Staples and Anthropologie. In recent months, it's brought on a growing stable of regional grocers, after announcing a partnership with Kroger last year. Instacart , which went public in 2023, was one of the biggest beneficiaries of a pandemic-driven surge in grocery delivery services, but it has struggled to maintain that momentum. In December Instacart agreed to pay $60 million to settle allegations by the Federal Trade Commission that it misled users with false advertising and deployed "unlawful subscription enrollment" practices. The service has also faced increasingly stiff competition from companies like Amazon and Walmart . After slowing its brick-and-mortar grocery effort, Amazon has doubled down on its online grocery business and leveraged its vast fulfillment footprint to speed up deliveries of household essentials, pantry staples and perishables. Both Amazon and Walmart have pushed further into same- and next-day delivery, which poses a threat to Instacart's on-demand delivery model. Analysts have noted that a potential combination of Instacart and DoorDash could attract antitrust scrutiny given the companies' market overlap. Third-party delivery platforms "remain a minority of total grocery consumption, but slicing and dicing the online market more narrowly or from a perspective of the grocers as enterprise customers can make approvals more challenging," Wedbush analysts wrote in a Monday research note. headlines.summary: Any button that can be clicked can also be touched.
headlines.article_text: Hands-on with Apple's first touchscreen laptop Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Apple announced its first touchscreen laptop models on Wednesday at an event in Los Angeles. Here's the good news for anyone who is worried about the new user interface: You don't have to use it. Apple said it used an oleophobic coating on its screens to resist fingerprints. It appears to work. In this article AAPL Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 1:59 01:59 Apple's new touchscreen Macbook Pro — first impressions News Videos Apple announced its first touchscreen laptop models on Wednesday at an event in Los Angeles. These new MacBooks, called MacBook Pro with ProLED XDR Display, are still Apple MacBooks. They run MacOS, not iPadOS or iOS, the iPhone's operating system. Here's the good news for anyone who is worried about the new user interface: You don't have to use it. Touch is entirely optional. CNBC briefly tested both the 14-inch and 16-inch touchscreen MacBooks at the event. Users can still primarily or entirely use the device's trackpad and keyboard, and there are few visual updates. MacOS still looks largely the same as it used to. Apple's touchscreen MacBook Pro with ProLED XDR Display. Andrew Evers | CNBC There have been a few user interface updates. For example, the red button on the top left of a window expands when you touch it to make it easier to click. Apple says that third-party developers like Microsoft and Adobe can and will update their apps to expand buttons and other touch targets to be larger. I think that touch will be particularly useful to scroll through websites or documents while lying down. But even software that hasn't been explicitly updated for the new computer will support touch. Apple says that behind the scenes, its software converts every touch tap into a traditional click. So any button that can be clicked can also be touched. Using the laptop with your finger feels good, but it won't change the way most people use their laptops. It could be useful for iPhone app developers, who can now test the way their apps work on their Mac. An accessibility feature allows users to pinch to zoom on any part of the user interface. Apple said on Wednesday that it had used an oleophobic coating on its screens to resist fingerprints. It appears to work. I didn't notice marks on the screen when I used the touch features. Apple is also, in addition to the touch feature, marketing these laptops as having a superior display, thanks to its new tandem OLED technology that offers deeper blacks and higher contrast. While photos and other art looked great on the screen, it's not a night-and-day difference from past Apple laptops. A lot of the improvements are aimed at creators who need accurate colors for photo and video editing. Apple's touchscreen MacBook Pro with ProLED XDR Display and 12MP Center Stage camera. Andrew Evers | CNBC Instead of the notch at the top of previous MacBooks, where Apple hides its cameras, the new MacBooks have a hole-punch cutout in the display, like recent iPhones. Apple's Dynamic Island feature — new to the MacBook — expands to show live activities and Siri. Apple made a big deal about the laptop's new hinge, which is meant to keep the screen from shaking when you touch it. For example, if you tap the screen on a video call, your camera won't shake as much. But the hinge feels largely the same as Apple's previous MacBook Pros. There is one new feature that is immediately noticeable and tells people you bought the latest, greatest, and most expensive Apple laptop. (The smaller 14-inch model starts at $2,899 and the bigger one costs at least $3,399.) The Apple logo on the lid now lights up when the computer is on. It's the first Apple laptop that supports it since the 2017 MacBook Air. Apple’s new touchscreen MacBook Pro. Andrew Evers | CNBC The light-up logo drew a cheer from analysts and influencers in attendance when it was announced on Wednesday.
